findings.minimum_fix: Mark each capability release attempted before the fallible operation, detach every callable/handle from active runtime use, keep immutable cached ledger and explicit unknown/pending outcomes, never retry a numeric fd or dlclose handle. A state free with unknown outcome must retain the driver capability and remain pending. Repeated close is observation/retry of explicitly safe disk operations only.
findings.static_counterexample: If driver dlclose succeeds and os.close(fd) raises after or without closing, _driver remains non-None. A second close invokes _ledger through an already unloaded driver, then may repeat dlclose and numeric-fd close. The stale call is earlier than the next close attempt.

findings.minimum_fix: Adopt per-image at-most-once native-release state and aggregate pending accounting before iterating. Preserve independent fd cleanup on loader failure without retrying either unknown release. Do not mark all native resources released solely because the dispatcher is closed.
findings.provenance: inherited pre-d5a AdaptiveRuntime behavior, newly inherited by the owner adapter; not introduced by the mapping patch
findings.static_counterexample: After one image fully closes and a later image release raises, _images still contains both and _closed remains false. Retrying close repeats release of the already closed earlier image. A per-image fd error after dlclose has the same stale-handle problem.

findings.static_risk: NativeRetirement deliberately closes the independently owned fd even when loader release is unknown. A still-retained old loader reference plus fd-number reuse can return a previous same-path mapping, particularly across different runtimes. Hashing the new sealed fd and finite output probes do not establish actual mapping identity. Upstream isolated test source explicitly exercises this loader behavior; this review did not run it.
